title: Crochet Hexagonal Bread Basket
positioning: kitchen and home (bread basket); small size only
required: partial_physical (a full make satisfies it and gives the #64 photograph)
cost_basis: gates.risk_matrix.owner_action_spec: 2.8 tester hours (estimate x1.3) at CA$20/h + 63 m yarn at CA$0.06/m. ESTIMATED ceiling; no tester has been paid yet
yarn_metres_scope: every piece the pattern makes (cir.twin._yardage x make)

materials.quantity: 1 ball (twin: 40.2 m needed; any ball of >= 50 m)

person_needed.who: one independent adult crocheter (not the owner, F-071) who agreed through the tester programme (quality.tester_programme)
person_needed.skill: confident with single crochet worked in joined rounds, increasing at six points to make a flat hexagon, and turning a base into straight walls; can read a written pattern in US terms; owns or can borrow a 1 g kitchen scale
person_needed.time: about 2-3 hours of making plus 15 minutes of measuring and recording

protocol: Before starting: weigh each full ball and record the ball band (grams and metres)
Work a 10 x 10 cm sc swatch first; record stitches and rounds per 10 cm and the hook; then RE-WEIGH each ball and use that as its start weight, so the swatch's yarn is not counted as project yarn
Make the basket exactly as written in the test PDF; note every place you had to guess, re-read or rip back, with the round number
Weigh what is left of each ball; grams used = re-weighed start minus end, per colour
Measure the finished base across the points and across the flats, and the wall height, in cm, without stretching

Set the empty basket on a flat table. Does the base sit flat without rocking? Does it hold its shape (walls upright, no collapse, lean or flare)? Answer yes or no to each, and write any problem in the problems box
Record total hours (not the swatch) and whether you followed the instructions exactly

Photograph in daylight on a real surface (wood, linen or a countertop). Keep every camera file UNEDITED: no filter, crop, resize or retouch; landscape or square, at least 2000 px each side, the whole basket in frame with space around it

Shots: (1) three-quarter view from about 30 degrees above, empty or with two or three rolls below the rim -- the listing's first photo; (2) straight down from above; (3) side view at table level; (4) a tape measure across the points, then a tape at wall height; (5) close-up of the rim and colour change; (6) in use on a set table with bread
Return the record sheet and the original photo files; the operator enters them (POST /api/physical-test and /api/physical-photo)

record_fields.label: base sits flat, no rocking? yes/no

covers_size.rule: a sample covers exactly this one size

intake.gate_opens_when: the physical.record job writes a PhysicalTest row with completed_at
intake.outcomes: PASS binds; PARTIAL (not flat, shape not held, a problem recorded) goes to the owner and binds nothing; FAIL binds nothing; a size outside 12% halts this release
